**Course Path for Project Management from Basics to Agile Delivery**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | EDX3326 | Advanced Project Management | edx | Foundational understanding of project management basics, including project life cycles, stakeholders, scope, time, cost, and quality management. |
| 2-4 weeks | EDX3248 | Agile Project Management | edx | Introduction to agile methodologies, including adaptive planning, facilitation of continuous improvement, assessment of project quality, and mitigation of risks. |
| 4-6 weeks | EDX3342 | Strategic Project Management | edx | Building on foundational and agile knowledge, this course covers strategic principles to effectively and successfully lead projects, including evaluating and selecting viable projects. |
| 6-8 weeks | EDX3229 | Project Management Foundations | edx | Reviewing the practical skills to address requirements like project scope, risk, time, and costs, and identifying challenges and improving processes to effectively manage project teams. |
| 8-10 weeks | EDX1778 | Strategic Applications of IT Project & Program Management | edx | Understanding the relationships among projects, programs, and portfolios, and defining the differences between predictive, iterative, and Agile-based lifecycles. |
| 10-12 weeks | EDX3283 | Oxford Leading Strategic Projects Programme | edx | Developing a set of personalized leadership skills to guide teams through uncertainty to successful project delivery, including managing potential project risks and capitalizing on opportunities. |
| 12-14 weeks | EDX219 | Project Management of Engineering Projects: Preparing for Success | edx | Understanding the importance of the front-end phases to create a successful project, including selecting an appropriate project manager and working together in a specialized project team. |
| 14-16 weeks | EDX1325 | Agile Process, Project, and Program Controls | edx | Controlling projects through actual measurements vs. estimates, and managing people, process, and product on empowered teams, including using Agile systems engineering to ensure valuable, integrated solutions. |
| 16-18 weeks | EDX2192 | Project Management Life Cycle | edx | Understanding the roles and responsibilities of a project manager, including project initiation and planning, project execution, and project closing. |
| 18-20 weeks | EDX1511 | Managing People with Power Skills | edx | Developing the prerequisites to review key interpersonal skills necessary to effectively manage projects, including defining stakeholders and interacting with them in predictive and adaptive environments. |
| 20-22 weeks | EDX1707 | Leadership and Management for PM Practitioners in IT | edx | Identifying personal and performance competencies for project management, building a plan for developing required project management competencies, and analyzing how team dynamics and culture can influence a project. |
| 22-24 weeks | EDX1346 | Applied Scrum for Agile Project Management | edx | Understanding why Agile is taking over, including history, case studies, and proof, and running a successful Scrum team for speed, innovation, leadership, and control. |
| 24-26 weeks | EDX62 | PM4R Agile: Agile mindset in development projects | edx | Understanding the characteristics and principles of the PM4R agile approach, a hybrid project management approach designed to apply agility in development and social impact projects. |
| 26-28 weeks | EDX821 | Effective Communication for Program and Project Stakeholders and Teams | edx | Explaining how to craft a clear and effective message, including the Understanding Triad: know-what, know-how, and know-why, and designing feedback to test for understanding by the audience. |
| 28-30 weeks | EDX3287 | Programme Management: A Monitoring and Evaluation Approach | edx | Understanding core abilities in M&E, and strategies for finance and resource tracking against desired programme goals, including practical tools to design, plan, and operationalise a programme. |
| 30-32 weeks | EDX635 | Risk Management in Development Projects | edx | Identifying the main stages involved in preparing a risk management plan for development projects, including recognizing the process of identifying risks and documenting their characteristics. |
| 32-34 weeks | EDX1986 | Agile Leadership Principles and Practices | edx | Understanding the key roles in Agile, including the Scrum Master, Product Owner, and Agile Team Member, and building self-organizing teams for Agile projects. |
| 34-36 weeks | EDX1275 | Sprint Planning for Faster Agile Team Delivery | edx | Understanding Kanban boards to limit work-in-progress (WIP) in a timebox, and time boxing activities to eliminate delays and gain schedule advances and ensure team capacity. |
| 36-38 weeks | EDX2132 | Storytelling That Delivers Program and Project Outcomes | edx | Explaining the structure and components of stories, creating a vision and status stories for a project or program, and utilizing stories to help manage risks and negotiate with stakeholders. |
| 38-40 weeks | EDX872 | Project Finance: Funding Projects Successfully | edx | Understanding how to create a financing structure that will provide the best chance of successful project financing, including the optimal allocation of roles, risks, and rewards between project stakeholders. |
| 40-42 weeks | EDX2491 | Project Management for Development | edx | Understanding basic project management concepts and techniques, including international standards, and widely tested tools and techniques that facilitate good communication within a project. |
